first_impression: The title screen and the sunset cutaways are lovely: low-poly pines against a peach sky, a little farmhouse with chimney smoke, sheep that look like popcorn clusters. In play it is mostly a high top-down view of a small dog trotting behind a small white blob. That works, but every evening ends up the same mauve-brown colour once the sun goes. There is clearly a real game here with a proper season structure. It just needs more punch on screen.
best_things: The sunset cutaways (03:27, 05:55, 08:02) and the title screen (00:00) are screenshot-worthy: a peach and rose sky over black pine silhouettes, chimney smoke and the fold below, and they mark the turn from calm to danger really well.

The season map (00:05, 01:20) gives a clear reason to keep going: ten named evenings across the year, each adding one new thing (lambs, Old Angus the ram, mist, a storm, first snow), plus stars, ribbons and charms to unlock.

The wolf snatch at 04:10-05:15 is real drama: a red banner with distance and seconds left, a picture-in-picture of the wolf dragging a lamb, a big red ring on the wolf, then 'Sheep rescued!' after the sprint across the burn.

worst_problems.problem: Past sunset the whole screen goes one muddy mauve-brown. Grass, heather, paths, rocks and the grey-blue wolves all sit on the same value, so the wolves read as smudges and you only find them by their red rings or edge markers.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep some contrast at dusk: let the grass stay darker and greener or bluer, and make the wolves clearly lighter or darker than the ground, so I can spot a wolf without reading a ring.

worst_problems.problem: Evenings just stop. The trial cuts from 'Time left 0:31' straight to the Lambing Time card, Lambing Time cuts at 'Nightfall in 0:08, 2 more to go' to the Old Angus card, and Old Angus cuts at 0:53 to Mist. No results screen, so I could not tell whether I won, lost or quit.
worst_problems.suggestion: Always show the end-of-evening card (stars, sheep home, lost to wolves) like the lovely one at 01:15. If I quit to the map, say so.

worst_problems.problem: The herding loop looks identical minute to minute: a tiny dog behind a tiny flock, seen from very high up. The Glenbrae Trial is the worst: two minutes of near-identical frames on a plain mown field.
worst_problems.suggestion: Bring the camera in closer by default, like the great close shots at 00:50-01:02 where the sheep and Pip actually have personality. Add more moments in the drive itself: sheep breaking off, a crowd reaction when a gate is cleared.

worst_problems.problem: The mist looks like a dirty lens: a grey wash over everything with a sepia-orange circle around Pip. It reads as a filter bug rather than fog rolling over a moor, and the flock, river and bridge all flatten into the same beige.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make the mist roll and drift with soft edges, and keep the clear area round Pip the true ground colour instead of tinting it orange.

worst_problems.problem: The HUD is busy and its text is tiny: a counter panel, timer bar, minimap, a full control bar along the bottom, a hint pill, top banners, edge icons and an inset camera all at once. During the snatch the red banner, inset and markers pile up.
worst_problems.suggestion: Hide the control bar once I know the keys, make the text bigger and fewer, and keep one clear alert at a time.

boredom_points: The Glenbrae Trial (01:27-02:52): a flat yellow-striped field, five sheep, a few gates, and the camera just watches a dog walk behind them for two minutes.
Old Angus around 06:12-06:32: Pip runs alone across empty heather and swims across the lochan looking for sheep, with nothing happening on screen.
The mist evening: the same grey-beige frame with a dog and a fuzzy flock for over a minute; even the bridge crossing at 08:35 is hard to make out.
confusions: Did I finish the trial or the lambing evening? Both cut away with time still on the clock and no result.
What the big yellow ring around Pip means (00:40, 07:15, and the double ring around Old Angus at 05:37). Is it a bark, a stare, or lying down?
The counter's rows of tiny dots and stars (for example '13, 15, 17' at 03:00) are too small to read at a glance.
Why the picture-in-picture shows a wolf in a pink and orange blur (04:10, 04:55); at that size I could not tell what was in it.
The many small round icons at the screen edges (sheep, house, wolf diamonds), especially the stack of sheep icons on the left in the mist (08:10-08:57).
wish_list: A closer, lower default camera, or one that pushes in during tense moments, so the animals have more character.
Real night: moonlight, a lantern, glowing wolf eyes, a darker blue instead of the mauve wash.
More reactions from the flock: a stray bolting, a ewe going back for her lamb, more bleats and panic you can see.
A results screen and replay highlight for every evening, including best times to beat.
A co-op mode with two dogs, or a whistle or handler mechanic.
Pip's coats or cosmetic unlocks shown somewhere in the menus (I only saw charms).
one_line_review: A pretty, cosy sheepdog game with a lovely sunset and a smart season structure, but the dusk turns everything to purple mush and the herding view is too far away to really feel it.
